newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japanese gold premiums plunge on traders' selling.
newsitem.headline: Japanese gold premiums plunge on traders' selling.

text.p: Gold prices in the Tokyo market plunged on Monday, falling below spot London market for the first time since June, due to active selling by some Japanese trade houses, traders said.
The spot Tokyo gold market was quoted at around 50 cents an ounce below spot London prices, against premiums of around 40-50 cents above spot London prices on a C and F basis last week, they said.
"Active selling, believed to be linked with Tokyo gold futures-related selling for position adjustment, pushed down spot Tokyo gold prices," a trading house trader said.
The gold premiums had been hovering around 40 to 50 U.S. cents on a C and F basis recently in sluggish trade, as weak gold demand depressed the market, they said.

Traders said, however, that the plunge in gold premiums in the spot Tokyo market would be temporary because the falls were mainly due to technical factors and not related to physical selling. They expected gold premiums to return to around 40 cents above spot London prices soon.
